issues.summary: Silent double-count on a supplier rename. greenBeanInvoices_ builds invoice_ref as `<supplierKey>/<invoiceNum>`, and supplierKey is only a trim/lowercase/whitespace-collapse of the free-text supplier cell (Order app Engine_CostApi.js costApiSupplierKey_). Editing that cell on an already-ingested invoice — e.g. fixing 'Coffee Co' to 'Coffee Co.' in 06_Stock_Intake — changes invoice_ref, so SUPPLIERS_KEY_COLS (source+invoice_ref) no longer matches and ingestSupplierRows APPENDS a second Suppliers row carrying the full invoice total while the old row stays. The snapshot diff finds no matching snap, classifies it as new, queues the week, and weeklySummarize then sums both rows: that week's greenbean spend silently doubles for the invoice, with no flag, warning or alert. docs/schema.md's stale-row runbook covers a DELETED intake row, not a renamed supplier on a still-present one, so an operator has nothing pointing at this. Either key on invoiceNum alone when it is non-blank, or detect an existing greenbean row whose invoice_ref shares the `/<invoiceNum>` suffix but differs in the supplier prefix and warn.

Docs still describe the online->source collapse rule that commit aa1921b deleted, and ingest-contract.md now contradicts itself inside one section. aggregateSupplierRows_ no longer collapses channel='online' revenue to one row per source — it `continue`s past those rows entirely. Three places still say otherwise: (1) docs/ingest-contract.md line ~52 'In the weekly Summary, channel: "online" is collapsed to one row per source' plus the bullet instructing a connector author to 'add it to the collapse rule in aggregateSupplierRows_', which no longer exists to edit — this sits ~10 lines below the new paragraph saying online is mechanically rejected; (2) docs/api.md line ~63 'location: "online" -> supplier is the source (shopify, ...), so online revenue is one row per source per week', naming a source retired in this same diff and describing a derivation that no longer happens (the only online Summary rows are shopify_orderapp direct writes); (3) the JSDoc immediately above aggregateSupplierRows_ (connectors/gas/Code.gs:1637-1643) still documents 'the SOURCE when channel is online'. Round 4 fixed exactly this class of contradiction in schema.md; the round-5 code change did not carry through to the other three.

validateIngest_'s coffee_order_app suppliers gate is an exact case-sensitive compare (`body.source === 'coffee_order_app'`, line 250) while the sibling online-revenue gate added three lines below it normalizes with String().trim().toLowerCase(). A payload declaring source 'Coffee_Order_App' or ' coffee_order_app' bypasses the suppliers rejection and ingests through the path docs/ingest-contract.md now calls mechanically rejected. The test suite only asserts the exact literal. Normalize both gates the same way.

greenBeanFetchAllRows_ accumulates diagnostics.warnings per page, but the producer recomputes that array over the whole matched set on every page rather than per page (Engine_CostApi.js costApiBuildReport_), so a multi-page pull collects N identical copies. The alert body then lists each warning N times and, worse, the suppression signature is `'warnings:' + upstreamWarnings.length` — so the same unchanged upstream condition produces a different signature whenever the page count changes, re-alerting on a condition that has not actually changed. Only reachable above 5000 matched rows, hence minor. Dedup the warning strings before counting.

greenBeanFetchAllRows_ dedups paged rows on rowNumber to survive rows being INSERTED into the live sheet between page fetches, but the opposite shift is unhandled: a row deleted mid-pagination slides the offset window forward and one row is never returned on any page, so the window ingests short with no signal. The existing paging.matched field would catch it — compare it against the deduped row count after the loop and log/abort on a shortfall. Same 5000-row reachability as above.

The flagged-row data-quality alert text is hardcoded to one cause: 'coerced values (non-numeric price/kg read as $0) ... likely UNDERSTATED'. The producer also pushes BLANK_SUPPLIER and INVALID_TIMESTAMP into the same rows[].flags array, and greenBeanPull_impl_ counts any non-empty flags array. A blank-supplier row therefore raises an alert telling Jake to go fix a price/kg cell that is fine. Bucket the count by flag value, or name the distinct flags present in the message.
